name: Accordion
summary: A vertically stacked set of interactive headings that each reveal a section of content. Modern HTML natively supports exclusive accordions with name="group" without JavaScript.
firstRuleExplanation: Under the First Rule of ARIA ("No ARIA is better than bad ARIA"), native <details> with <summary> is vastly superior for standard document and content disclosure. Modern browsers support exclusive accordions natively using the name attribute on multiple <details> tags (opening one closes the others). The APG ARIA pattern requires custom buttons, aria-expanded, aria-controls, role="region", and custom JavaScript keyboard event handlers.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Expands or collapses the focused accordion panel via JS handler.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Natively opens or closes the <details> disclosure without JS.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Moves focus to next accordion header button.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Moves focus to next <summary> or interactive child.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Moves focus between accordion trigger buttons (optional APG enhancement).
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Standard tab navigation; arrow keys navigate within text.

ariaRequirements: Heading tag (e.g. <h3>) wrapping each trigger <button type="button">
aria-expanded="true/false" maintained via JavaScript on every click/keydown
aria-controls="panel-id" pointing to the unique ID of the expandable panel
Panel marked with role="region" and aria-labelledby="button-id"
Panel hidden attribute or CSS display:none synchronized with expanded state
Custom JavaScript event listeners for click and keyboard triggers

keyboard: Enter / Space: Toggles expanded/collapsed state via JavaScript listener
Tab / Shift+Tab: Moves focus sequentially between trigger buttons and open panel focusables
Arrow Down / Up: Moves focus across triggers (optional APG enhancement)
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces "button, Billing Information, expanded [or collapsed], region Billing Information".

ariaEffort.summary: Requires manual state synchronization, event listeners, and attribute management on every toggle.

semanticRequirements: Native <details> parent tag and <summary> heading element
name="group-name" attribute on each details element to enforce exclusive single-panel opening
0 lines of JavaScript needed for toggling, state management, or exclusive accordion behavior

keyboard: Enter / Space: Natively toggles summary open/closed state
Tab / Shift+Tab: Natively navigates to next summary or active panel content
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Natively announces "details, collapsed [or expanded], Billing Information, summary" via browser accessibility tree.

semanticEffort.summary: Built directly into the browser engine in C++. Completely functional with JavaScript disabled.

semanticLimitations: Default browser disclosure triangle marker requires ::marker or ::-webkit-details-marker CSS reset.
Historically difficult to animate height smoothly (now supported in modern browsers via interpolate-size: allow-keywords and @starting-style).

Heading hierarchy inside requires placing heading tags within summary (

).

tips: Use summary::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; } and list-style: none on summary to remove default arrows across all engines.
Target details[open] summary to change background or rotate custom indicator icons.

semanticCode.notes: Using name="faq-group" makes details elements exclusive: expanding one automatically collapses all others in the same group natively!

name: Dialog (Modal)
summary: A modal dialog overlays the main view and requires user interaction before returning. The native HTML <dialog> provides top-layer rendering, native focus trapping, Esc closing, and automatic backdrop styling.
firstRuleExplanation: Implementing an accessible modal dialog with ARIA from scratch is notoriously error-prone: you must manage a backdrop div, trap keyboard focus within the dialog, handle the Esc key, mark all background DOM nodes as inert or aria-hidden="true", and restore focus to the trigger on close. Native <dialog>.showModal() does ALL of this in the browser engine natively.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Must be manually trapped inside dialog via JS keydown listener.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Browser automatically traps focus inside <dialog> natively.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Must be caught manually via JS to close dialog and return focus.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Natively fires cancel/close event and closes modal.

ariaRequirements: Container element with role="dialog", aria-modal="true", and aria-labelledby="title-id"
Fixed viewport backdrop <div> element
JavaScript focus trap: intercepting Tab/Shift+Tab to keep focus within dialog focusable nodes
Marking all page siblings with inert or aria-hidden="true" while modal is open
JavaScript keydown listener for Escape key to close modal
Tracking opener button in document.activeElement and restoring focus upon close

keyboard: Tab / Shift+Tab: Trapped within dialog, cycling between first and last focusable element
Escape: Closes dialog and returns focus to opener button
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces "dialog modal, Confirm Deletion". Assistive tech virtual reading cursor must be confined to dialog content.

ariaEffort.summary: Focus trap leaks and missing background inerting are among the most common web accessibility failures.

semanticRequirements: Optional <form method="dialog"> to close modal natively on button click without JS

keyboard: Tab / Shift+Tab: Automatically trapped inside modal by browser engine
Escape: Natively fires cancel event, closes dialog, and restores focus to invoking element
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces native dialog role, title, and isolates reading order to the dialog natively.

semanticEffort.summary: Browser Top Layer handles z-index, backdrop, focus containment, and inertness natively.

semanticLimitations: Calling dialog.show() creates a non-modal dialog without focus trap or backdrop; dialog.showModal() must be used for modals.
Animating entry and exit transitions requires modern CSS (@starting-style and transition-behavior: allow-discrete).
Positioning relative to triggering element as a flyout requires CSS Anchor Positioning or manual offset calculation.

tips: Always style dialog::backdrop directly rather than injecting custom backdrop divs.
Use method="dialog" on nested forms for zero-JS button dismissals.

name: Switch
summary: A toggle control representing a binary on/off state. Standard HTML checkbox supports role="switch" for exact AT announcement while preserving native form submission and keyboard interaction.
firstRuleExplanation: Developers often create custom <div> or <button> switches with ARIA, requiring manual click, spacebar, and enter handlers, plus custom state tracking. Using a native <input type="checkbox" role="switch"> leverages native checkbox form submission, native keyboard behavior, and native assistive technology support while announcing itself as a switch.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Toggles aria-checked between "true" and "false" via JS listener.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Natively toggles checked state without any JS.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Often handled manually in custom button switches.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Natively submits enclosing form if in form context.

ariaRequirements: <button type="button" role="switch" aria-checked="false"> or <div role="switch" tabindex="0">
JavaScript click and keydown (Space/Enter) handlers
Updating aria-checked="true/false" attribute dynamically
Does NOT submit in standard HTML <form> without hidden input

keyboard: Space: Toggles switch state between true and false
Enter: Toggles switch in button context
Tab: Moves focus to the switch
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces "switch, Notifications, on [or off]".

ariaEffort.summary: Requires custom state tracking and hidden form inputs for form integration.

semanticRequirements: Submits natively in HTML forms (submits name=on when checked)

keyboard: Space: Natively toggles checked state
Tab: Focuses native checkbox
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Natively announces "switch, Notifications, checked [or not checked]".

semanticEffort.summary: Native checkbox behavior with switch role announcement.

semanticLimitations: Browsers render <input type="checkbox" role="switch"> as a standard square checkbox unless styled with CSS appearance: none.
Form submission sends the value only when checked (standard checkbox behavior).

tips: Use appearance: none directly on the input[type="checkbox"][role="switch"] to avoid extra span wrapper markup while keeping full focus visibility intact.

semanticCode.notes: Fully keyboard accessible, participates in HTML form validation and submission, and works with JavaScript disabled.

name: Slider
summary: A user input where the user sets a value from a given range. Native <input type="range"> provides full keyboard, mouse, touch, and screen reader support without JavaScript.
firstRuleExplanation: The APG ARIA slider requires building custom track and thumb markup, managing aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, tracking mouse dragging, touch movements, and listening for ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, ArrowUp, ArrowDown, PageUp, PageDown, Home, and End keys. Native <input type="range"> provides all of this out of the box with zero JavaScript.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Decreases aria-valuenow by step size via custom script.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Natively decreases slider value.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Increases aria-valuenow by step size via custom script.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Natively increases slider value.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Sets aria-valuenow to minimum / maximum via custom script.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Natively sets slider to min / max.

ariaRequirements: <div role="slider" tabindex="0" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="100" aria-valuenow="50">
Custom track element and draggable handle element
Mouse drag listener, Touch move listener, pointer capture
Keydown listener for ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, ArrowUp, ArrowDown, PageUp, PageDown, Home, End
Does not participate in HTML form submit without hidden input

keyboard: Arrow Left / Down: Decrements value by step
Arrow Right / Up: Increments value by step
Page Up / Down: Increments / decrements by large step (e.g. 10)
Home / End: Jumps to minimum / maximum values
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces "slider, Volume, 50%, min 0, max 100". Updates on every step.

ariaEffort.summary: Requires touch, mouse, pointer, and keyboard coordinate math and bounding box calculations.

semanticRequirements: Built-in <output> element for live visual value display
0 lines of JavaScript needed for slider operation

keyboard: Natively supports all arrow keys, PageUp, PageDown, Home, and End without a single line of JS.
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Natively announces range slider, current value, min, max, and orientation.

semanticEffort.summary: Complete accessibility, keyboard, touch swipe, and mouse drag built into the browser engine.

semanticLimitations: Cross-browser thumb and track styling requires two separate vendor prefixes (::-webkit-slider-thumb and ::-moz-range-thumb).
Dual-fill track styling (highlighting the completed portion of the track) is not natively standardized and requires CSS linear-gradient or accent-color.

tips: accent-color: #color is supported in all modern browsers and styles the native slider thumb and filled track with 1 line of CSS!

apgCode.html: Volume:

semanticCode.html:
<!-- Semantic HTML5 Range Input -->
<label for="sem-vol">Volume:</label>
<input type="range" id="sem-vol" name="volume" min="0" max="100" value="50">
<output for="sem-vol">50</output>
semanticCode.notes: Native range inputs automatically support touch dragging, scroll wheel increments, mouse clicks, and all keyboard navigation.

name: Meter
summary: A graphical display of a numeric value within a known range, such as disk usage or battery level. The native HTML <meter> element includes semantic understanding of optimum, low, and high thresholds.
firstRuleExplanation: The native <meter> element communicates scalar measurement and gauge semantics directly to assistive technologies. It also provides built-in attributes for min, max, low, high, and optimum, allowing browsers and user agents to convey whether a gauge is in a favorable or alert status. The ARIA role="meter" requires custom styling, manual aria-valuenow updates, and cannot natively represent the optimum range concept.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Meters are read-only; not focusable unless embedded in interactive context.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Non-focusable read-only semantic element.

ariaRequirements: <div role="meter" aria-valuenow="70" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="100" aria-label="...">
Custom track container + custom fill <div> with inline style="width: 70%"
Manual color updating logic in JS to change colors if value enters warning/critical zones

keyboard: Not focusable (read-only scalar display)
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces "meter, Disk Usage, 70 percent".

ariaEffort.summary: Must manually compute percentages, fill widths, and color thresholds.

semanticRequirements: <meter min="0" max="100" low="33" high="66" optimum="80" value="70">70%</meter>

keyboard: Read-only native element; skipped by Tab sequence
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Natively announces meter value and whether reading is optimum, suboptimal, or alert.

semanticEffort.summary: Native browser scalar gauge with built-in optimum heuristics.

semanticLimitations: Browser default styling renders native OS appearance, which looks drastically different between Windows, macOS, and Linux.
Custom styling requires resetting -webkit-appearance and targeting vendor pseudo-elements (::-webkit-meter-bar, ::-webkit-meter-optimum-value).

tips: Include fallback text inside the <meter> tag (<meter value="70">70%</meter>) for older user agents.

apgCode.html: Disk Usage:

semanticCode.html:
<!-- Semantic HTML5 Meter -->
<label for="disk-meter">Disk Usage:</label>
<meter id="disk-meter" min="0" max="100" low="30" high="80" optimum="20" value="78">
  78%
</meter>
semanticCode.notes: Browser renders native threshold color changes (green/yellow/red) based on low, high, and optimum attributes.

name: Button
summary: The primary interactive control for triggering actions. The classic demonstration of the First Rule of ARIA: a <div> with role="button" requires extensive custom JavaScript to replicate native <button>.
firstRuleExplanation: A native <button> element comes with automatic keyboard activation (both Space and Enter fire click), native focusability, native disabled state (which prevents click and keyboard events), form integration (type="submit", type="reset"), and standard accessibility API mapping. An ARIA fake button (<div role="button" tabindex="0">) requires manual keydown listeners for Space and Enter, custom disabled management, and often fails in screen reader virtual cursor modes.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Must be caught in JS keydown to invoke the button action.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Natively fires the click event on <button>.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Must be caught in JS keydown, e.preventDefault() called to prevent page scroll, and action invoked on keyup.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Natively triggers button on keyup; page does not scroll.

ariaRequirements: <div role="button" tabindex="0">
Keydown listener for Enter to invoke action
Keydown listener for Space to call e.preventDefault() (prevent page scroll) and invoke action on keyup
Manual :focus-visible styling
Manual disabled state management (aria-disabled="true" and tabindex="-1")
Does NOT submit forms without manual form submission JS

keyboard: Enter: Triggers button action
Space: Triggers button action (must prevent window scroll)
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces "button, Save Changes".

ariaEffort.linesOfCode: ~30 lines of JS + CSS to duplicate native button
ariaEffort.summary: Common source of bugs where Space key causes page scroll or disabled buttons still trigger.

keyboard: Enter and Space natively trigger click event without scrolling
Disabled attribute prevents all focus and click events automatically
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Natively announces button role and accessible name.

semanticEffort.summary: The epitome of the First Rule of ARIA.

semanticLimitations: Default browser button styling has legacy borders and backgrounds; requires standard CSS reset (border: none; background: transparent; font: inherit).
Buttons default to type="submit" inside a <form> if type attribute is omitted.

tips: Always specify type="button" on non-submitting buttons to prevent accidental form submissions!

apgCode.html: Save Changes

semanticCode.html:
<!-- Semantic HTML Button -->
<button type="button" class="btn-primary" onclick="doAction()">
  Save Changes
</button>
semanticCode.notes: Requires 0 lines of helper code. Fully accessible, keyboard responsive, and form-aware out of the box.

name: Link
summary: An interactive hyperlink that navigates to a new resource or location. Native <a> elements provide essential browser features that fake ARIA links cannot replicate.
firstRuleExplanation: Using <span role="link" tabindex="0"> breaks standard web browser functionality: users cannot middle-click or right-click to "Open link in new tab", "Copy link address", or bookmark the URL. Search engine spiders cannot crawl fake links. Native <a href="..."> provides full browser navigation, context menus, and accessibility natively.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Must catch keydown in JS and manually set window.location.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Natively follows the hyperlink.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Does NOT show "Open in new tab" or "Copy Link Address".
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Shows full native browser hyperlink context menu.

ariaRequirements: <span role="link" tabindex="0">
JavaScript click listener to set window.location.href
JavaScript keydown listener for Enter key to trigger navigation
Fails to provide browser context menus (Open in new tab, Copy link)

keyboard: Enter: Navigates via JS handler
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces "link, Privacy Policy".

ariaEffort.summary: Breaks browser fundamental behaviors (middle-click, right-click, bookmarking, SEO).

keyboard: Enter: Natively follows hyperlink; Shift+Enter opens in new window; Cmd/Ctrl+Click opens in new tab
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Natively announces link, URL target, and visited status.

semanticEffort.summary: Native HTML hyperlink.

semanticLimitations: Missing href attribute turns <a> into a non-interactive placeholder link without keyboard focus or link role.

tips: Never omit href on <a> tags if keyboard interactivity is expected.

apgCode.html: View Privacy Policy

semanticCode.html: View Privacy Policy
semanticCode.notes: Supports right-click, middle-click, command-click, bookmarking, hover status URL preview in browser bar, and screen reader links lists.

name: Radio Group
summary: A set of checkable buttons where no more than one button can be checked simultaneously. Native radio buttons provide single tab-stop roving focus and arrow navigation natively.
firstRuleExplanation: The APG ARIA radio group pattern requires manually implementing roving tabindex (managing tabindex="0" on the selected radio and tabindex="-1" on all others), listening for ArrowUp, ArrowDown, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, and updating aria-checked. Native <input type="radio" name="..."> grouped by a <fieldset> with <legend> provides this entire behavior natively with zero JavaScript.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Focuses the checked radio button (tabindex="0").
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Focuses the checked radio button in the group.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: JS updates tabindex="-1", sets next radio to tabindex="0", and updates aria-checked="true".
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Natively checks and focuses previous radio in the group.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: JS updates tabindex="-1", sets next radio to tabindex="0", and updates aria-checked="true".
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Natively checks and focuses next radio in the group.

ariaRequirements: <div role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="title-id">
<div role="radio" tabindex="0/-1" aria-checked="true/false">
Roving tabindex algorithm across all 4 arrow keys
Manual state sync and focus setting in JS

keyboard: Arrow Up / Down / Left / Right: Moves focus and checks selected radio
Tab: Moves focus to the checked radio button (single tab stop)
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces "radio button, checked 1 of 3, Shipping Speed".

ariaEffort.summary: Must manually implement roving focus and keyboard traversal that HTML does natively.

keyboard: Natively provides single tab stop for group and arrow key selection across all browsers.
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces legend as group context, then radio button label, state, and position (1 of 3).

semanticEffort.summary: Native browser implementation.

semanticLimitations: Default browser radio circles have rigid OS styling unless overridden with accent-color or appearance: none.

tips: Always wrap native radio groups in <fieldset> with <legend> so screen reader users hear the group prompt before the option.

<!-- Semantic HTML Radio Group -->
<fieldset class="semantic-radiogroup">
  <legend>Subscription Tier:</legend>
  <label>
    <input type="radio" name="tier" value="monthly" checked>
    Monthly ($9)
  </label>
  <label>
    <input type="radio" name="tier" value="annual">
    Annual ($89)
  </label>
</fieldset>
semanticCode.notes: Grouped under a semantic legend for assistive tech context; arrow key navigation works across all browsers natively.

name: Checkbox (Tri-State / Mixed)
summary: A control that allows the user to toggle between checked, unchecked, or partially checked (mixed/indeterminate) states. Native checkbox handles the mixed state via the DOM indeterminate property.
firstRuleExplanation: While creating a custom checkbox (<div role="checkbox">) requires writing custom Space key listeners and focus styling, the native <input type="checkbox"> handles focus, toggling, and form submission natively. For parent "select all" checkboxes that need a mixed state, setting the DOM property checkbox.indeterminate = true provides native screen reader mixed state announcements without abandoning native checkbox semantics.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Cycles aria-checked between "false", "true", and "mixed" via JS.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Natively toggles checked state.

ariaRequirements: <div role="checkbox" tabindex="0" aria-checked="mixed">
Custom SVG or font icon for checkmark and minus icon
JavaScript Space key listener to cycle between false -> true -> mixed

keyboard: Space: Cycles between checked, unchecked, and mixed
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces "checkbox, partially checked [mixed], All Permissions".

ariaEffort.summary: Manual rendering of tri-state icons and keyboard space listeners.

semanticRequirements: JavaScript setting checkbox.indeterminate = true for parent status

keyboard: Space: Natively checks or unchecks checkbox
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Natively announces "checkbox, partially checked / mixed".

semanticEffort.summary: Leverages native OS tri-state rendering and accessibility tree states.

semanticLimitations: The indeterminate state CANNOT be set via HTML markup alone (e.g. there is no indeterminate HTML attribute); it MUST be set via JavaScript property: input.indeterminate = true.

tips: Use the :indeterminate CSS pseudo-class to style parent checkboxes when in the mixed state.

apgCode.html: All Permissions

semanticCode.html:
<!-- Semantic HTML Checkbox with Indeterminate Property -->
<label>
  <input type="checkbox" id="sem-parent-box">
  All Permissions
</label>

name: Disclosure (Show/Hide)
summary: A simple button that controls the visibility of an associated section of content. Modern HTML <details> and <summary> provide this natively with zero JavaScript.
firstRuleExplanation: The disclosure pattern is one of the most common web interactions. Before HTML5 <details>, developers used <button aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="content">. Native <details> provides complete keyboard accessibility, automatic aria-expanded state handling, built-in search-on-page text matching (browsers automatically expand details when searching with Ctrl+F), and zero JavaScript overhead.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Toggles aria-expanded and panel visibility via JS.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Natively toggles details open state.

ariaRequirements: <button type="button" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="content-id">
<div id="content-id" hidden>
Click event listener to flip aria-expanded and hidden

keyboard: Enter / Space: Toggles expanded/collapsed state via JS
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces "button, collapsed [or expanded], What is WCAG 3.0?".

ariaEffort.summary: Requires synchronizing aria-expanded attribute with panel hidden state.

keyboard: Enter / Space: Natively toggles details open state
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Natively announces "details, collapsed [or expanded]".

semanticEffort.summary: Standard HTML5 disclosure.

semanticLimitations: Browsers render default black triangle arrow that requires removal via CSS.

tips: Details contents automatically expand when users search with browser Find (Ctrl+F)!

semanticCode.html:
What is WCAG 3.0?

WCAG 3.0 is the upcoming draft standard for web content accessibility guidelines.

name: Combobox / Autocomplete
verdictLabel: Native Preferred for Basic; ARIA for Rich Popups
summary: A composite widget combining a single-line textbox with an associated popup listbox. Native <datalist> provides zero-JS autocomplete, while APG Combobox is needed for rich custom dropdowns.
firstRuleExplanation: For standard text suggestion and search autocomplete, the native HTML <datalist> element paired with an <input list="..."> provides built-in keyboard navigation, native OS suggestions, and screen reader announcements with zero JavaScript. The APG Combobox pattern is only warranted when dropdown options require rich HTML markup (avatars, subheadings, badges) or multi-select chip tags.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Opens popup listbox and moves focus or aria-activedescendant.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Opens native datalist suggestion menu.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Selects active option and closes listbox via JS.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Fills selected suggestion into input.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Closes listbox and resets focus to input.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Dismisses suggestion dropdown.

ariaRequirements: <input role="combobox" aria-autocomplete="list" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="list-id">
<ul role="listbox" id="list-id"> with <li role="option">
Managing aria-activedescendant or roving tabindex
Listening for ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Enter, Escape, Home, End
Filtering list items dynamically on text input

keyboard: Arrow Down: Opens popup list and moves active descendant
Enter: Selects active option and closes list
Escape: Closes popup listbox and keeps input focus
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces "combobox, expanded / collapsed, option 1 of 5".

ariaEffort.summary: Requires intricate keyboard focus management, virtual cursor tracking, and ARIA syncing.

keyboard: Arrow Down: Natively opens suggestion dropdown
Enter: Selects highlighted suggestion
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Natively announces available suggestions and input auto-complete.

semanticEffort.summary: Zero-JS native autocomplete provided by browser.

semanticLimitations: Option items in <datalist> CANNOT be styled with custom CSS or contain rich HTML (avatars, icons, secondary descriptions, badges).
Dropdown presentation is controlled entirely by the operating system / browser UI.

tips: When simple string autocomplete is needed, use <datalist>. Switch to the APG Combobox pattern ONLY when options require rich media or multi-column layouts.

<datalist id="standards-list">
  <option value="WCAG 2.2">
  <option value="WCAG 3.0">
  <option value="Section 508">
  <option value="EN 301 549">
</datalist>
semanticCode.notes: Supported in all modern browsers without any script. Provides native fuzzy matching and assistive technology integration.

name: Menu Button / Popover
verdictLabel: Native Popover API Preferred for Navigation
summary: A button that opens a flyout menu. The APG Menu pattern is designed for desktop-style application command actions; for site navigation, the modern HTML Popover API is preferred.
firstRuleExplanation: One of the most widespread accessibility anti-patterns on the web is using ARIA role="menu" and role="menuitem" for site navigation links. In ARIA, a menu is an application menu (like File/Edit in a desktop app) where Tab exits the menu and Arrow keys navigate items. When applied to website dropdowns, screen reader users expect arrow navigation and cannot tab through links. Modern HTML provides the Popover API (popover, popovertarget) which gives native top-layer flyout and light-dismiss without ruining link semantics.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Opens application menu and focuses first menuitem.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Natively opens popover panel.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: In APG Menu, Tab immediately closes menu and moves to next page element!
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Tabs sequentially through all interactive items inside popover.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Closes menu and returns focus to menu button via JS.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Natively closes popover (light dismiss).

ariaRequirements: <button aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false"> + <ul role="menu"> + <li role="menuitem">
Arrow Up/Down navigation within menu
Esc to close and return focus
Tab immediately closes menu and moves to next page element

keyboard: Enter / Space: Opens menu and focuses first item
Arrow Down / Up: Navigates menuitems
Escape: Closes menu and focuses button
Tab: Closes menu immediately
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces "menu button, has popup menu, expanded / collapsed".

ariaEffort.summary: Frequently misimplemented on web navigation links where Tab navigation is broken.

keyboard: Enter / Space: Opens popover
Escape: Natively closes popover (light dismiss)
Tab: Traverses all interactive elements inside popover normally
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces button trigger and top-layer popover panel.

semanticEffort.summary: Browser Top Layer with light-dismiss built in.

semanticLimitations: Popover API is supported in modern browsers (Chrome 114+, Firefox 125+, Safari 17+); older legacy browsers require polyfill.

tips: Use the Popover API for flyouts and dropdowns that contain navigation links, and reserve ARIA role="menu" only for desktop-like application action palettes.

semanticCode.notes: Native Popover API renders in the browser Top Layer, features light-dismiss (clicking outside or pressing Esc closes it), and preserves standard Tab order.

name: Tabs
semanticElement: No native <tabs> element exists in HTML
summary: A set of layered panels where only one panel is displayed at a time. Because HTML currently lacks a native <tabs> element, the APG Tabs pattern remains the required accessible pattern.
firstRuleExplanation: Unlike dialogs, accordions, and sliders, HTML does not have a native <tabs> or <tabpanel> element (although WHATWG and OpenUI have active proposals). Therefore, implementing tabbed interfaces requires following the W3C APG Tabs pattern: role="tablist", role="tab", role="tabpanel", aria-selected="true/false", and roving tabindex with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight navigation. Some developers attempt hacks using radio buttons or details, but only the APG ARIA pattern communicates true tabbed semantics to screen readers.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Moves focus from active tab directly into the tabpanel content (single tab stop for tablist).
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Without ARIA tabs, every tab is an independent tab stop.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Moves focus between sibling tabs and (in automatic mode) activates the panel.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Not supported without custom ARIA script.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Moves focus to the first or last tab in the tablist.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Not supported without custom ARIA script.

ariaRequirements: <div role="tablist" aria-label="..."> container
<button role="tab" aria-selected="true/false" aria-controls="panel-id" id="tab-id">
<div role="tabpanel" id="panel-id" aria-labelledby="tab-id" tabindex="0">
Roving tabindex algorithm (active tab has tabindex="0", inactive have tabindex="-1")
ArrowLeft / ArrowRight keyboard listeners to switch tabs
Tab key jumps from active tab directly into tabpanel content

keyboard: Arrow Left / Right: Navigates between tabs (roving focus)
Tab: Jumps directly into active tabpanel content (single tab stop for tablist)
Home / End: Focuses first / last tab
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces "tab, selected [or unselected], tab 1 of 3". Tabpanel announces associated tab label.

ariaEffort.summary: Normative standard required because HTML does not have a native <tabs> element.

semanticRequirements: NO native <tabs> element exists in HTML specification yet!
Can be approximated using <details name="tab-group"> or CSS-only radio buttons, but neither communicates true tab semantics to assistive technologies.

keyboard: Without ARIA, each tab button is a separate tab stop (violating expected tablist keyboard efficiency).
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announced as individual buttons or details, lacking tab / tabpanel relationship.

semanticEffort.summary: Use the W3C APG ARIA Tabs pattern.

semanticLimitations: HTML has no native tab widget. WHATWG and OpenUI are developing proposals, but none are standardized.
Radio-button tab hacks pollute form data and fail to represent tabpanel relationships to screen readers.

tips: Always keep tabpanel focusable (tabindex="0") if it contains no focusable interactive children, so keyboard-only users can scroll long content.

semanticCode.html: Spec Status: WHATWG & OpenUI have active proposals for <tabs>. Until standardized, the W3C APG ARIA Tabs pattern above is the normative industry standard.
semanticCode.notes: Always ensure your tablist is treated as a single tab stop, with arrow keys switching tabs, and Tab jumping directly into the tabpanel.

name: Table vs Data Grid
verdictLabel: Native Table Preferred; ARIA Grid for Apps
summary: A tabular presentation of data. Native HTML <table> provides built-in screen reader navigation commands; ARIA role="grid" is reserved for interactive spreadsheet applications.
firstRuleExplanation: Native HTML <table> with <th> scope="col/row" and <caption> gives screen reader users built-in matrix reading shortcuts (e.g. Ctrl+Alt+Arrows in JAWS/NVDA, VO+Arrows in VoiceOver). Replacing tables with <div role="table"> is unnecessary work. Furthermore, developers often misuse role="grid" when they simply have a data table: role="grid" tells assistive technologies to disable standard table navigation in favor of arrow-key cell traversal, which should only be used for interactive widgets like spreadsheets or calendars.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Works if role="table", role="row", role="cell" are all configured.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Natively supported across all screen readers.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Moves active cell focus in 2 dimensions across rows/columns.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: In standard <table>, arrow keys scroll or navigate text.

ariaRequirements: <div role="table">, <div role="rowgroup">, <div role="row">, <div role="columnheader">, <div role="cell">
For role="grid", 2D arrow key cell traversal must be programmed manually with roving tabindex

keyboard: Arrow keys navigate cells in role="grid"
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Screen readers must emulate table commands on custom divs.

ariaEffort.summary: Complete reinvention of standard HTML table elements with zero usability benefit for static data.

keyboard: Screen reader users navigate rows and columns with native shortcuts (Ctrl+Alt+Arrows)
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Natively announces table dimensions (e.g. "table with 4 columns and 10 rows") and reads column headers automatically.

semanticEffort.summary: Native browser HTML table.

semanticLimitations: Responsive tables on narrow mobile screens require horizontal overflow wrappers (overflow-x: auto) to avoid breaking layout.

tips: Always use <th scope="col"> and <th scope="row"> to ensure header cell associations are unambiguous.

name: Spinbutton
summary: A stepper input for selecting a numeric value from a defined range. Native <input type="number"> provides native stepper controls, mobile numeric keyboards, and keyboard navigation.
firstRuleExplanation: The APG ARIA spinbutton requires a <div> with role="spinbutton", aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, plus increment and decrement buttons and custom keydown listeners for ArrowUp, ArrowDown, PageUp, PageDown, Home, and End. Native <input type="number"> does all of this natively and automatically triggers numeric keypads on mobile smartphones.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Increments / decrements aria-valuenow via JS.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Natively increments / decrements input value by step size.

ariaRequirements: <div role="spinbutton" tabindex="0" aria-valuenow="1" aria-valuemin="1" aria-valuemax="10">
Increment & decrement trigger buttons
Keydown listeners for ArrowUp and ArrowDown
Manual state sync and display text updating

keyboard: Arrow Up / Down: Increments / decrements number value
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces "spinbutton, Quantity, 3".

ariaEffort.summary: Manual implementation of number stepping and constraint checking.

keyboard: Arrow Up / Down: Natively increments / decrements number by step
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Natively announces spinbutton with min, max, and current value.

semanticEffort.summary: Native browser number input.

semanticLimitations: Different browsers render different native stepper spinner arrows; hiding them requires vendor CSS rules.

tips: Native <input type="number"> triggers numeric keypads on iOS and Android automatically.

<input type="number" id="sem-qty" name="quantity" min="1" max="10" step="1" value="1">
semanticCode.notes: Automatically provides native stepper buttons, handles min/max constraints, and opens numeric keypad on iOS/Android.

name: Landmarks
summary: Structural landmarks define major regions of a webpage, allowing screen reader users to jump directly between sections. HTML5 landmark elements map natively to ARIA landmark roles.
firstRuleExplanation: Never use <div role="banner"> or <div role="main"> when you can use <header> and <main>. Modern HTML provides explicit elements for every major ARIA landmark: <header> (banner), <nav> (navigation), <main> (main), <aside> (complementary), <footer> (contentinfo), and the modern <search> element (search).

keyboardMatrix.key: Screen Reader Landmark Shortcut (D key in JAWS/NVDA)
keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Navigates to role="banner", role="main", etc.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Natively jumps to <header>, <main>, <nav>, <aside>, <footer>.

ariaRequirements: <div role="banner">, <div role="navigation">, <div role="main">, <div role="contentinfo">
Manual role assignment on generic div containers

keyboard: Screen reader shortcut keys (D or R) jump between landmarks
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces "banner", "main", "navigation".

ariaEffort.summary: Redundant when HTML5 landmark tags are available.

keyboard: Screen reader shortcut keys (D or R) jump between HTML5 sections natively
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Natively maps to accessibility landmark roles in all screen readers.

semanticEffort.summary: Zero effort landmark architecture.

semanticLimitations: <header> and <footer> only map to banner and contentinfo when they are direct children of <body> (not scoped within <article> or <section>).

tips: Use aria-label on <nav> elements (e.g. <nav aria-label="Main Navigation">) to distinguish multiple navigation landmarks on the same page.

name: Breadcrumb
summary: A navigation trail showing the user’s location within a hierarchical site structure. The standard pattern combines semantic HTML <nav> and <ol> with aria-current="page".
firstRuleExplanation: The breadcrumb pattern represents the ideal synergy between semantic HTML and ARIA. Semantic HTML provides the container (<nav>), the ordered sequence of steps (<ol> and <li>), and the hyperlinks (<a>). ARIA provides the critical attribute aria-current="page" on the active link or element, informing assistive tech users that they are currently on that step.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Tabs sequentially through each breadcrumb link.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Tabs sequentially through each breadcrumb link.

ariaRequirements: <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">
<ol> ordered list containing <li> items
aria-current="page" on the final link or span

keyboard: Tab: Moves sequentially through breadcrumb items
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces "Breadcrumbs navigation, list 3 items", and on current item announces "current page".

ariaEffort.summary: Clean hybrid pattern requiring only aria-current="page".

keyboard: Tab: Moves through links in sequence
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces ordered navigation trail and current page step.

semanticEffort.summary: Pure HTML list with one ARIA attribute.

semanticLimitations: HTML has no native breadcrumb element or current-page attribute; aria-current="page" is universally required.

tips: Use a <span> with aria-current="page" for the last item rather than an <a> tag to avoid confusing unclickable self-links.

name: Tree View
verdictLabel: ARIA Required for App Trees; Nested Details for Docs
summary: A hierarchical list with parent and child items that can be expanded and collapsed, typical in IDE file trees and file managers.
firstRuleExplanation: For true application file explorer widgets, the APG Tree View pattern (role="tree", role="treeitem", aria-expanded) is required to deliver the expected single-tab-stop roving focus and hierarchical arrow navigation (ArrowRight expands/enters child, ArrowLeft collapses/jumps to parent). For simple hierarchical reading documents or site maps, nested <details> and <summary> elements provide an accessible zero-JS alternative.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Expands closed tree item, or moves focus to first child if already open.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: In <details>, Space/Enter toggles.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Collapses open tree item, or moves focus to parent item if closed.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: In <details>, standard cursor navigation.

ariaRequirements: <ul role="tree">, <li role="treeitem" aria-expanded="false">, <ul role="group">
Roving tabindex across entire tree hierarchy
ArrowRight: expands or descends into children
ArrowLeft: collapses or ascends to parent
ArrowDown / ArrowUp: moves sequentially through visible items

keyboard: Arrow keys navigate tree levels with roving tabindex
Enter / Space activates item
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces "treeitem, level 1, expanded 1 of 4".

ariaEffort.summary: Hierarchical roving tabindex and recursive expand/collapse tracking.

semanticRequirements: Nested <details> and <summary> tags for document trees

keyboard: Enter / Space: toggles open/closed
Tab: moves to next focusable element
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces disclosure levels natively.

semanticEffort.summary: Zero JS nested document tree.

semanticLimitations: Nested <details> lacks the single-tab-stop roving focus expected in desktop application file managers.

tips: For reading content and sitemaps, nested details is vastly simpler and requires zero maintenance.

name: Carousel
verdictLabel: Hybrid: CSS Scroll Snap + Semantic Buttons
summary: A rotating or scrollable showcase of cards, images, or slides. Modern CSS Scroll Snap combined with semantic HTML buttons provides a high-performance, touch-friendly alternative to complex ARIA carousels.
firstRuleExplanation: The APG Carousel pattern involves complex ARIA live regions, role="roledescription", pause/play controls, and tablists. In modern web development, CSS Scroll Snap (scroll-snap-type: x mandatory) allows developers to build native momentum scrolling with GPU acceleration. Semantic <button> elements provide previous/next navigation and announced status without fragile custom DOM math.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Tabs through slides or controls depending on tablist mode.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Tabs sequentially through prev/next buttons and slide items.

ariaRequirements: <section role="region" aria-roledescription="carousel" aria-label="...">
Slides marked with role="group" and aria-roledescription="slide"
aria-live="polite" / "off" region container
Pause / resume rotation button (WCAG 2.2.2 requirement)

keyboard: Tab moves through slides; pause button stops rotation
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces "carousel, slide 1 of 3".

ariaEffort.summary: Complex live region timing and rotation management.

semanticRequirements: Scroll container with CSS scroll-snap-type: x mandatory
0 lines of JavaScript needed for touch swipe and momentum scrolling

keyboard: Arrow keys scroll slides natively when scroll container is focused; Tab moves to next button
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces native button controls and slide list items.

semanticEffort.summary: CSS Scroll Snap gives GPU-accelerated touch swipe natively.

semanticLimitations: Automatic rotation requires JavaScript (and pause controls to meet WCAG 2.2.2).

tips: CSS Scroll Snap works on mobile touch devices with zero JS drag math.

name: Alert
summary: A time-sensitive message that communicates important information to the user without receiving focus. HTML <output> natively maps to a polite live region, while role="alert" provides assertive interruption.
firstRuleExplanation: For general form feedback and calculated results, the native HTML <output> element provides an automatic live region with role="status" and aria-live="polite". When an urgent error or critical notification requires immediate screen reader interruption, the ARIA role="alert" (equivalent to aria-live="assertive") is specifically required.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Alerts are NOT focused; screen readers announce automatically.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Output elements are not focused; announced via live region.

ariaRequirements: <div role="alert"> (or aria-live="assertive" + aria-atomic="true")
Container must exist in DOM before content is dynamically injected

keyboard: Not in Tab sequence; does not receive focus
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Immediately interrupts speech to announce alert content.

ariaEffort.summary: Requires dynamic DOM node injection into existing live container.

keyboard: Not focusable; passive status container
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Politely announced when output value changes.

semanticEffort.summary: Native HTML output tag.

semanticLimitations: <output> announces politely; it cannot assertively interrupt a screen reader during urgent critical errors (where role="alert" is needed).

tips: Never place role="alert" on elements with keyboard focus; alerts are designed for passive non-focused announcement.

semanticCode.notes: <output> natively maps to an accessible live region that notifies screen readers when content changes.

name: Tooltip
summary: A contextual popup that displays information describing an element when focused or hovered. Modern CSS Anchor Positioning and Popover API dramatically simplify accessible tooltips.
firstRuleExplanation: The native HTML title attribute has significant accessibility defects: it does not work on touchscreens, cannot be resized, does not support custom contrast or keyboard delays, and violates WCAG 1.4.13 (Content on Hover or Focus). The APG pattern using aria-describedby and role="tooltip" remains essential, but modern CSS Anchor Positioning (anchor()) and the Popover API (popover="hint") now make the visual anchoring robust and pure CSS.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Dismisses the tooltip without moving keyboard focus (WCAG 1.4.13).
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Popover API natively dismisses hint on Esc.

ariaRequirements: <button aria-describedby="tip-id">
<div role="tooltip" id="tip-id" hidden>
Event listeners for mouseenter, mouseleave, focus, blur, and Escape key dismissal

keyboard: Focus reveals tooltip
Escape dismisses tooltip without losing focus (WCAG 1.4.13)
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Reads tooltip text as accessible description after the button label.

ariaEffort.summary: Requires coordinate math to avoid edge clipping and timer management.

semanticRequirements: 0 lines of JavaScript needed with title

keyboard: Hover or focus shows native tooltip in some browsers (unreliable in title)
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Reads title attribute if no other description exists.

semanticEffort.summary: Native title attribute.

semanticLimitations: The HTML title attribute CANNOT be styled with CSS, does not work on mobile touchscreens, cannot be zoomed without page zoom, and cannot be dismissed with Escape in many browsers (violating WCAG 1.4.13).

cssCustomization.ariaRecipe: [role="tooltip"] { position: absolute; background: #000; color: #fff; padding: 4px 8px; border-radius: 4px; }
tips: Never put essential information only in a tooltip; always ensure primary instructions are visible on screen.

name: Toolbar
summary: A collection of commonly used controls arranged in a single tab stop where users navigate with arrow keys.
firstRuleExplanation: In complex applications (e.g. rich text editors), having 20 formatting buttons create 20 separate Tab stops severely degrades keyboard navigation efficiency. The APG Toolbar pattern groups related controls into a single tab stop: Tab enters the toolbar, Arrow keys navigate between controls, and Tab exits to the next document element.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Enters or exits the entire toolbar as a single unified tab stop.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Without toolbar, each button is a separate tab stop.

keyboardMatrix.apgAction: Moves roving focus between buttons in the toolbar.
keyboardMatrix.semanticAction: Does nothing between standard buttons.

ariaRequirements: <div role="toolbar" aria-label="Formatting">
Roving tabindex across buttons (first button has tabindex="0", others have tabindex="-1")
ArrowLeft / ArrowRight listeners to cycle focus
Home / End to jump to first / last button

keyboard: Arrow keys navigate toolbar buttons; Tab exits entire toolbar
ariaKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces "toolbar, Formatting".

ariaEffort.summary: Required for complex applications to prevent Tab key fatigue.

keyboard: Each button is an individual Tab stop in standard HTML
semanticKeyboardAndAt.screenReader: Announces fieldset legend and individual buttons.

semanticEffort.summary: Standard HTML button group.

semanticLimitations: HTML button groups have no built-in roving tabindex; every button requires a Tab press, creating keyboard navigation clutter in tool-dense apps.

tips: Use role="toolbar" in rich applications (like text editors or drawing canvases) to keep the tab order clean.

semanticCode.notes: For simple forms, separate tab stops are acceptable; for rich apps, the APG roving toolbar is essential.
